elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 6(c) expressly permits Customer, defined as Company, to terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience-termination right is available without restriction based on an outstanding Statement of Work or committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 6(c) makes the right exercisable “at any time,” with no outstanding-Statement-of-Work limitation.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its convenience-termination right on 30 days' notice.
Customer's convenience-termination notice must be written.
Contractor must refund prepaid fees following Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 6(c) requires Contractor to refund prepaid fees upon such termination.

elements.element: The refund must be calculated pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: Section 6(c) expressly provides a pro-rata refund for the period after termination becomes effective.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 2 establishes no separate fixed committed Agreement term, and Section 6(a) permits Contractor convenience termination only when no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding. Contractor therefore cannot exercise that right during an active Statement-of-Work commitment.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 6(c) expressly grants Customer a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 6(c) requires only 30 days' notice, which is outside the stated fallback range of 60–90 days, although it is more favorable to Customer.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged to Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so the conditional cap is satisfied.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination-for-convenience right may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 6(a) permits Contractor to terminate whenever no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding; it does not expressly limit termination to the end of an Agreement or Statement-of-Work term.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 6(a) requires Contractor to give 90 days' advance written notice.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position: Customer receives an unrestricted 30-day written convenience right and pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, while Contractor cannot terminate during an active SOW commitment. The fallback is not independently satisfied because Customer's notice period is not within 60–90 days and Contractor's right is tied to the absence of an uncompleted SOW rather than expressly to the end of a term. The change is not minimal because extending Contractor's notice from 15 to 90 days was unnecessary to achieve the preferred level, though it remains related to the same termination subject. Unrelated breach, payment, and work-product provisions are preserved without contradiction.
